speaker_notes.note: The student's 'prosperity gospel' framing is a provocative analogy for trying to win divine notice by indirect self-assertion. The roughness is part of the student's speech, not Jiang's wording.
ASR alternates between 'Ricarda,' 'Picardo,' and related variants for Piccarda. Jiang is still discussing Piccarda's place in Paradise.

interactions.summary: Jiang keeps pressing a student to explain how changed will would actually work, and the answer begins to shift from fear-driven good behavior toward a contingent will that aligns with the soul's higher will.
Students try out self-worth and stronger aspiration as the route to redemption, while Jiang dismisses indirect begging or mere contentment and keeps demanding a concrete act of will toward God.

Jiang resolves the problem by saying redemption would mean actively willing ascent toward God; that stronger will displays faith, love, and trust, whereas attributing one's low sphere to God is an insult because one's cosmic place is chosen through free will.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the student's direction only once changed will means more than good conduct: the decisive shift is the contingent will coming into harmony with the soul's higher or absolute will.
A student proposes that indirect attempts to get God to notice you through good works are still a disguised form of begging rather than genuine spiritual transformation.
Jiang says the concrete path to redemption would be to intensify the will to ascend closer to God rather than to compensate with charitable or familial good deeds.
For Jiang, exercising more will toward God is itself evidence of faith, love, and trust, which is what God actually wants from the soul.
Jiang argues that no external power assigns a soul its place in the universe; wherever a person is, that station is there because the person chooses it through free will.

Jiang says Piccarda insults God when she treats her low sphere as something God chose for her and thanks him for it, because that reading denies her own agency and wrongly attributes the limitation to God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes redemption a matter of daring to want more nearness to God instead of trying to compensate through niceness or philanthropy.
signature_moments.source_phrase: God wants you to love yourself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns repentance from moral bookkeeping into a charged act of self-affirming faith.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang radicalizes free will by saying every cosmic station is self-chosen rather than assigned from above.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Wherever you are in the universe, it's because you choose to be there
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's hardest claim about responsibility and explains why blaming God is spiritually false.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang flips pious gratitude into offense by saying Piccarda insults God when she claims God placed her in the lowest sphere.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures the lecture's reversal from passive acceptance to active responsibility for one's nearness to the good.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for the soul's situational or lower willing, which must be brought into harmony with the higher will rather than left fear-driven.

chronology_notes.note: The packet completes the move from anti-consequentialism to a full voluntarist reading: redemption is not compensatory action but the soul's stronger willing toward God, and low placement is reinterpreted as self-chosen rather than divinely imposed.
